A continuous engineering investment in the JHEEM ecosystem, with one destination:

**Status:** Working program vision for team review; the destination and priorities will be refined with the team.

> **The path from a new policy question to a published, reproducible answer on jheem.org becomes weeks of pipeline instead of months of hand work.**

Today that path has two very different halves. At the delivery edge, container artifacts are golden-tested and promoted by digest, simulation data ships as semantically versioned releases, and a modern web portal serves the results. Upstream, where the science is produced, the workflow remains artisanal: a ~75,000-line engine with no automated test gate, no CI, and no README; fifteen model applications, each roughly 10–15,000 lines of standalone scripts adapted by hand from a predecessor; one data-manager pipeline whose assembly, validation, and promotion run in CI but whose raw-data stage remains local; other managers built locally end to end; and calibrations that run for days as black boxes. Every published result crosses this boundary ([Anatomy of a Model Application](application-anatomy.qmd) documents the crossing in detail).

The program is the work of moving that wall leftward until the whole path is a production line.

## Where this goes

The end state, roughly two years out:

- **A new model application starts from a scaffold, not a copy.** Specification, likelihoods, parameters, and interventions have declared places; the marginal cost of application #16 stops being ten thousand hand-adapted lines.
- **Calibration is an observable, managed process.** Submit a specification and data; watch per-city likelihoods and mixing on a monitor; get a versioned simset release out the other end — the same release discipline `jheem-simulations` already has, extended upstream to the thing that produces the releases.
- **Every data manager builds through the completed raw-to-final syphilis pattern**: pinned inputs, regression-gated, promoted — so the left edge of the pipeline is as governed as the right.
- **jheem2 is a real package**: installable, documented with runnable examples, tested — learnable by a new student in an afternoon, adoptable by another lab at all.
- **Every number on jheem.org or in a paper is a build artifact.** Portal → simset release → calibration run → data-manager version → raw-data release → code refs. "Can you reproduce Figure 3" is answered with a tag and one command.

The measure of the program is **time from policy question to reproducible published answer**. When a funding change or policy proposal hits the news, the team that can say "here is what it does to HIV incidence in 32 cities, and here is the tag that reproduces it" in three weeks — instead of a quarter — is doing different science.

## Why this is achievable here

Because the strongest pattern already exists here. The container platform's build → test-by-digest → promote pipeline runs today and provides a complete internal exemplar; the syphilis manager's gated assembly-and-promotion path is a partial upstream exemplar whose raw-to-final path remains to be completed. The program is not "adopt best practices" in the abstract — it is extend working practices already demonstrated inside this ecosystem backward through calibration, data, and the engine itself.

## Why now: verification compounds

Automated verification is a prerequisite for faster onboarding, safer maintenance, and credible AI-assisted work. A plausible change to a large engine file still requires the same evidence regardless of who or what drafted it. Without an automated gate, an expert must re-derive that evidence by hand exactly where the code is hardest.

The toy model, CI, executable documentation, ecosystem map, and runbooks all reduce that re-derivation cost. Their primary value is safer, more legible engineering; they also allow AI-assisted contributions to be evaluated through the same tests and review standards as any other contribution. Verification is what turns additional implementation capacity into useful capacity rather than additional review burden.

## The line, in three stretches

The line gets built along **one production path first**: a single reference application taken end to end — raw data to published artifact — then extracted as the paved road the other fourteen follow. This guards against the failure mode of a cleaner engine package while the actual scientific workflow stays artisanal.

Each concrete capability below was raised by someone on the team. Statuses link to the [roadmap](roadmap.qmd), which is the working tracker; on this page, **shipped** is reserved for capabilities installed in their durable home, used through the supported path, and guarded against regression.

### 1 — Make it verifiable *(in progress)*

- **The toy model** — a complete, self-contained JHEEM model that runs in 0.37 seconds ([details](toy-fixture-spike.qmd)). **Spiked and verified (GO)**; it ships when it lands in jheem2 as a package fixture executed on every change, which is the first step of CI. It is the first application built the way all of them eventually will be: minimal, self-contained, executable anywhere — the seed of the test suite, the runnable documentation, and the application scaffold.
- **Changes to shared code, proven safe** — CI on jheem2: package build plus the toy model producing *exactly* the same numbers, on every proposed change. **Next up.** This flips the economics of small fixes: the unfinished corners everyone notices become safe to fix in passing.
- **Watch calibrations while they run** — a read-only monitor over the checkpoint files the MCMC machinery already writes: per-city likelihood behavior, chain mixing, which cities are struggling, while the run is going. **Next up.** (Automatic stopping of non-mixing runs comes later, once the test net exists to touch the sampling loop safely.)

### 2 — Make it fast

- **One loading path** — export the functions specs actually use, so `library(jheem2)` works for everyone and the per-session C++ recompile (the source of "same code, different machine, different result" — including a real R 4.4 vs 4.5 crash) goes away.
- **Documentation that answers questions** — reference pages and tutorials whose examples *execute* against the toy model, so they can never silently go stale. Onboarding becomes: read the [ecosystem map](ecosystem-map.qmd), run the quickstart, have a full specify → simulate → plot loop working on day one.
- **Data managers graduate to CI** — the syphilis pipeline (whose assembly, validation, and promotion stages already run gated in CI) is completed raw-to-final, then census and surveillance managers adopt the finished pattern; "which data, which code, which result" always has an exact answer.
- **An application scaffold** — the copy-adapt ritual replaced by a template with the toy model as its worked example.

### 3 — Make it compound

- **Full provenance** — the question-to-answer path reproducible end to end from a tag.
- **Managed calibration** — submit, observe, stop, resume; results land as versioned releases.
- **An ecosystem others can build on** — jheem2 as a documented, tested package usable beyond the lab, with a supported contribution path grounded in executable evidence.

## How the work runs

- **Small slices, continuously.** No rewrites, no long-lived branches, no "freeze while we refactor." Every increment lands within days and the models keep working throughout.
- **Something visible every couple of weeks** — a monitor, a guide, a fixed annoyance — not just internal scaffolding.
- **At most two things in flight.** A deliberate work-in-progress cap keeps the program from sprawling.
- **The team steers.** The [roadmap](roadmap.qmd) is reviewed and re-ranked with the team; anything not paying off gets cut.
- **Safety before surgery.** Changes that could affect model results wait until the automated checks exist to prove they didn't. Nothing about this program bets the science on an untested change.

## Already landed

- First fixes on jheem2 `dev`: a method-registration bug that had forced a workaround in the interactive app, two engine crashes found by the toy-model spike, repository cleanup.
- The **toy model** itself — spiked, verified (GO), and already paying for itself in bugs found.
- This site: the [ecosystem map](ecosystem-map.qmd), a working [specification reference](spec-framework-notes.qmd), the [decision log](decisions.qmd), and the program's running record.
- The templates were already here: the container platform's digest-promotion gates and the syphilis manager's gated CI assembly-and-promotion path are in-house proof of the practices stretches 2 and 3 extend.

## What it costs

The program starts small, earns further investment by shipping useful capabilities, and remains interruptible as scientific priorities change. The team's role is to steer at reviews: reinforce what pays off, re-rank what matters next, and cut what does not.
